header:
What difference does
a **flat payment** make
on a credit card?
footer: 24% APR · minimum = 1% + interest, $35 floor · no new charges

vo.text: Six thousand dollars on a card at 24%.
Pay the minimum: about eighteen years, and ten thousand in interest.
A flat $200 a month: under four years. About $7,200 less.
Just $20 more than the first minimum: fourteen years sooner.

verdict.text:
Just **$20** more than the first minimum:
**≈ 14 years** sooner

lever.text:
= $200 − $180 = **$20** more a month
≈ 14 years sooner than the minimum

notes: Stress variant: 4 options, the first already run at frame 1 (t 0); long behaviours (the fitter drops them to the working lines) and long deltas with no room in the titles or under the values: they stand on the money row beside their own values (the 'beside' place, clear of his reach; the winner steps back before his jump), to the last frame, and bump when read at 16.4; mixed payoff units on one time axis (≈ 18.3 years vs 47 / 26 / 14 months: the fast plans barely leave the start line and their saved-time strips run most of the lane); a 2-line footer; 2-line working lines; captions off; resultT on option 2 (a 2.4 s lead-in: he strains and the crate trembles before it gives) and deltaT; a counted money value (from the minimum's); a lever across lanes 0 and 1; reads of a crate, a money value and two deltas. Lands in the col layout, money at 60 px. The header breaks in three balanced lines (no one-word orphan). Maths: $6,000 at 24% APR (2% a month), no new charges, simulated month by month (re-checked in Python): minimum = 1% of the balance + that month's interest, $35 floor; first payment $60 + $120 = $180; 219 payments (18.25 years ≈ 18.3), interest $10,441.80. Flat $200: 47 payments, $3,254.63 ($7,187.17 less; 219 − 47 = 172 months ≈ 14.3 years sooner). Flat $300: 26 payments, $1,739.24 ($8,702.56 less). Flat $500: 14 payments, $929.90 ($9,511.90 less).
